lines.text: Summer came to Greyhollow. It had never really come before. The old women said the north had always had two seasons. Winter, and almost winter.
Now the fields were gold with barley. The glasshouses stood open to the sun. And for three peaceful weeks, I forgot what my father had said.
Then Wren came back from a hunt, pale and out of breath.
Riders on the south road. Twelve of them, in blue robes, with silver lenses round their necks. Two days away. Maybe less.
Blue robes. Silver lenses. Measurers. The Royal Order of the Measure.
And for some reason, when Wren said it, both Bram and our scholar went completely still.
Lord Lucan. We need to talk. Now. Privately.
She took off her spectacles and put them on the table. Then she took something from her satchel. A silver lens, exactly like the ones Wren had described.
My name is Ilse Thorne. I am not a scholar. I am a Royal Measurer. The Order sent me here to find you.
Find me? Why? I'm a zero. Everyone knows that.
The night after your Measuring, the Stone in the capital cracked. Straight through its heart.
A stone doesn't crack because it finds nothing, my lord. It cracks because it can't hold what it finds.
I didn't understand. I said so.
You don't have a Vessel. You have something else. Something that pours. Everything you take responsibility for, grows. Your land. Your animals. Your people.
When you arrived, every person in this village measured one ring. Now not one of them is below two. Wren is at four. Tobin is at four. Bram is at five.
Bram is at five?
Since midwinter, my lord.
You knew?
Since the morning the dog came home bigger than a horse.
I sat down. The mill. The glasshouses. The wolves. Wren's arrow through the tree. Bram, one-armed, cutting down a frost-wolf in one stroke. Oswin's frost, against my brother's fire.
So the soil was fine.
The soil was fine, my lord.
The Order has a name for what you are. Hollow-born. They have hunted your kind for three hundred years. Those twelve riders are not coming to measure you, Lucan.
They are coming to take you.
Outside the window, the barley moved in the wind. A hundred and twelve people were bringing in the harvest. Every one of them mine.
And every one of them, I realised, was now in danger. Because of me.
Then they'll have to get past Greyhollow first.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter fifteen, coming soon.
